A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching authors, methods and principal experiments. Text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM gameplay, behavioral-model fitting, baseline comparisons and supplementary analyses in Section 4 and Appendix B, alongside analysis of an existing human dataset.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a payoff-rescaling evaluation of the Gemini 2.5 Flash behavioral model in Appendix B.2.

M1.justification: The AlphaEvolve discovery procedure, likelihood and Halstead objectives, SBB selection rule and five appendix programs are substantively unchanged. Printing the existing template in the main text and adding a workflow diagram do not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: Appendix B.2 adds a limited test scenario with tenfold IRPS payoffs for the Gemini 2.5 Flash SBB program. The human population, four LLMs, 15 bots and underlying game coverage remain unchanged; the passage does not establish new gameplay collection.

E2.justification: The evaluated behavioral-model comparators remain Nash equilibrium, CS-EWA and the GRU-based RNN. The gameplay figures retain random/Nash and oracle references. The new payoff test introduces no additional comparison method.

E3.justification: The added robustness evaluation multiplies payoffs by ten and measures cross-validated likelihood. Existing collection settings, data partitioning, fitting procedures, hyperparameter searches and primary metrics are retained. This is an additional evaluation condition, not evidence that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.2 tests the Gemini 2.5 Flash SBB program's sensitivity to reward scaling. The earlier analyses of conceptual prevalence and offline reproduction of gameplay statistics remain, renumbered as B.3 and B.4.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same independent trials, random-initialization procedures, 95% confidence intervals and Bonferroni-corrected Wilcoxon tests. The new payoff result supplies no additional seed information, uncertainty estimate or statistical procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds a cross-validated likelihood of 0.462 under tenfold payoffs, compared with the retained original-data value of 0.491 for Gemini 2.5 Flash. This is a new condition-specific result. Existing main and supplementary plotted results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The game and behavioral-model definitions, SBB rule in Equation 1, likelihood objective in Equations 2–3, CS-EWA algorithms and Halstead formulas are retained. Mathematical differences are typesetting changes; no new proof or substantive derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract and three headline contributions remain unchanged. Section 5 nevertheless strengthens 'not perfect proxies' for human behavior to 'not proxies' and replaces the emphasis on strategic-reasoning scenarios with broader decision-making scenarios.

C2.justification: v2 adds explicit caution about interpreting digital-twin studies, proposes internal-state probing and logit analysis to investigate the discovered mechanisms, and discusses social-partner benefits and negotiation risks. The distinction between predictive models and ground-truth mechanisms was already present in v1.

D1.justification: Existing implementation and access information is substantively retained, including preprocessing, prompts, optimization settings, data access and all five SBB programs. The newly displayed main-text template already appeared in v1 Appendix E.4; Figure 12 illustrates the previously documented workflow.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and positioning against prior behavioral modeling and LLM studies are retained. Bibliographic changes, including the Capraro publication update and corrected Amble/Cohen attribution, concern existing works rather than an expanded literature base or revised novelty claim.

P1.justification: v2 renames Section 2, revises parts of the discussion, adds conflict-of-interest and impact statements, and removes the acknowledgements. Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact, with limited explanatory and editorial revisions.

P2.justification: The document is extensively reformatted from the Google report style to the ICML proceedings style, changing the title and abstract arrangement, typography, captions, table spacing and code pagination. v2 also adds Figure 12 and repeats the template as main-text Listing 1. Existing result displays are retained and rescaled or relocated.

improvement.justification: The new workflow diagram, clearer captions and explicit conflict disclosure improve readability and transparency, while Appendix B.2 adds a focused check of reward-scale sensitivity. These gains are limited: the check covers one program without uncertainty reporting, and the broader proxy language exceeds the scope of the retained IRPS evidence. The core findings and reproducibility material remain stable.
